hero.title: Frontend Engineer - KeksOwl
hero.heading: Frontend Engineer focused on interactive UI, product thinking and engineering quality.
hero.mainText: I work on complex product interfaces where frontend is not just presentation, but part of the product itself — interaction design, responsiveness, accessibility, usability and the long tail of details that shape how software feels in everyday use.
hero.mainTextSecond: Most of my work lives somewhere between engineering, UX and product thinking: building interactive tooling, refining workflows, improving interface clarity and creating interfaces that feel reliable, responsive and intuitive over time.
hero.subText: Currently working with TypeScript, React and modern frontend tooling on complex interactive surfaces at Songsterr.

about.title: About
about.mainText: Hi! I'm Semyon, or just Keks — a {role} who treats UI as a system, not a set of screens. I think about how components scale, how state flows, how an interface holds up when the network drops or a screen reader takes over. The kind of work where engineering decisions shape what the user feels — even if they never notice.
about.mainTextSecond: I work well in teams that blur the line between design and engineering — where both sides care about the result, not just the handoff. Whether it's two people or twenty, what matters to me is honest code review, async-first communication, and enough documentation that decisions don't get lost between sprints.
about.mainTextThird: Outside of work I run tabletop RPG campaigns, build FoundryVTT modules, and translate video games and rulebooks from English to Russian. Turns out localization is just frontend with higher stakes: one wrong word and your bard starts a diplomatic incident.

composition.title: Composition
composition.text: Components that work together, not just in isolation. How state flows between modules matters more than how any single one looks inside.

product.title: Product thinking
product.text: The best frontend work starts before the ticket. Understanding why something exists shapes how it should feel.

craft.title: Craftsmanship
craft.text: Details compound. Tooltip timing, focus order, empty states, loading sequences — the sum of small decisions is what users call 'polish'.

ownership.title: Ownership
ownership.text: If I shipped it, I see it through. From first deploy to steady state — that's when the interesting edge cases surface.
